items.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023
items.q: He was first entranced with jazz when he listened to “West End Blues,” Louis Armstrong — Louis Armstrong’s “West End Blues” in London.

ctx.x: Do you think that some of the African-American musicians thought of him differently even though he’s white but he was British, that maybe he didn’t bring any of the prejudice that was so apparent at that time?

Yeah. That’s a good question, and I believe they did think of him differently for that reason. He was first entranced with jazz when he listened to “West End Blues,” Louis Armstrong — Louis Armstrong’s “West End Blues” in London. And then when he came over to the States and he was able to meet him he was just so bowled over that these people he admired treated him with such friendliness and he was shocked. I don’t know what the situation was at the time in London, but my dad was horrified at the racial prejudice…
Did you become aware — when did you become aware that your name had significance? I’ll just leave it at that. What they chose to name you.
